body: Both came of age in a small, pre-electronic, poorly regulated Dalal Street (BSE ring trading, badla carry-forward, no insider-trading regulations before 1992, and SEBI only getting statutory powers in 1992). There, broker networks, sentiment reading and access to promoters were real information edges. Some of that access later sat at or past the line, as Aptech (2016) shows. Retail investors today face faster price discovery, disclosure rules and insider-trading enforcement. What remains replicable is temperament and business analysis, not the network.

body:
**Morningstar "Mind the Gap" (US 2025 edition, 10 years to 31 Dec 2025)**
- Dollar-weighted investor return of about 8.7% a year vs total fund return of about 9.9%, a gap of about 1.2 points a year, roughly 12% of the return. — [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/business/insights/research/mind-the-gap-2025)
- Least-volatile funds had a gap of about −0.4%, the most volatile about −2.1%. The gap is wider for ETFs than for open-end funds, narrowest for allocation and target-date funds, and active vs passive is *not* the main driver. — [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/business/insights/research/mind-the-gap-2025); [Advisor Perspectives 2026](https://www.advisorperspectives.com/commentaries/2026/08/21/what-advisors-can-learn-from-the-investor-return-gap)

**DALBAR QAIB**
- 2025 QAIB (calendar 2024): average equity investor +16.54% vs S&P 500 +25.02%, an 848 basis-point gap, the second largest in a decade. — [DALBAR 2025 press release](https://www.dalbar.com/Portals/dalbar/Cache/News/PressReleases/2025QAIBPressRelease.pdf)
- 2026 QAIB (calendar 2025): investor 17.16% vs S&P 500 17.88%, a 0.72-point gap, the smallest since 2012. — [DALBAR 2026 press release](https://www.dalbar.com/PressReleases/doc/2026QAIBReportPressRelease.pdf)
- **Caveat:** DALBAR's methodology has been criticised by academics and by Morningstar, so Morningstar's dollar-weighted figures are the more conservative source. The size of the DALBAR gap varies wildly from year to year.

**India**
- Axis MF, 2003–2022: equity and hybrid funds returned about 19.1% a year, the average investor earned about 13.8%, and a hypothetical SIP earned about 15.2%. Axis is a fund house and has a commercial interest. — [Axis MF "Thinking Aloud"](https://www.axismf.com/cms/sites/default/files/pdf-factsheets/Thinking%20Aloud%20-%20Using%20your%20Mutual%20Funds%20More%20Effectively.pdf)
- Value Research studied 170 diversified equity funds over 10 years, using actual investor cash flows. The gap ranged from 1% to about 10%. Reported via Mint; I did not open the original. — [Mint via Magzter](https://www.magzter.com/en/stories/newspaper/Mint-New-Delhi/WHY-DO-YOUR-RETURNS-RARELY-MATCH-WHAT-FUNDS-DELIVER)
- Morningstar India example: a top fund returned 40% over 3 years, but the average investor earned 20%, because about 75% of the inflows arrived in the final year. — [Morningstar India](https://www.morningstar.in/posts/69884/why-does-the-funds-return-differ-from-yours.aspx)
- Advisorkhoj: investor returns trailed both point-to-point and SIP returns in equity, hybrid, and debt funds. Stopping SIPs during corrections defeats their purpose. — [Advisorkhoj](https://advisorkhoj.com/news/Mutual-Fund/MFs%20Investor%20Returns%20vs%20Fund%20Returns)

body:
`person:group-sterling-sandesara` · flag: **severe** · confidence: verified · tickers: STERLINGBI

Flag: SEVERE. Gujarat gelatin/pharma group (Sterling Biotech, also oil & gas via Nigerian blocks) whose promoters Nitin and Chetan Sandesara (and Deepti Sandesara) left India in 2017 as CBI and ED pursued alleged bank fraud on an Andhra Bank-led consortium (agency figures ranged from ~Rs 5,000 cr to ~Rs 14,500 cr+ including overseas lenders). Sterling Biotech's listed equity was effectively wiped out in insolvency/liquidation. ED attached assets including Nigerian oil assets. Resolution: in Nov-2025 the Supreme Court accepted a government-placed sealed-cover proposal and ordered that all criminal proceedings (CBI, ED, SFIO) would be quashed once Rs 5,100 cr was deposited by 17-Dec-2025 -- stressing it is not a precedent (OTS amounts for Indian and foreign-guarantor companies were cited as Rs 3,826 cr and Rs 2,935 cr). In 2026 the Supreme Court questioned SEBI for continuing its proceedings and later told it to close the case or face action (Apr-2026); lenders sought release of funds from the court registry. Investor read: settlement extinguishes criminal exposure for promoters, not losses of minority shareholders. Early signals at the time: aggressive capacity expansion in a niche product (gelatin), large overseas subsidiaries, related-party transactions with promoter-owned firms, and a diary/ITs raid (2011) naming payments. Lesson: 'settlement' outcomes in India can let promoters exit cases -- governance history must be judged on conduct, not on criminal outcomes.

- **regulator findings:** criminal cases quashed by SC on Rs 5,100 cr deposit (Nov-2025)

Sources:
- <https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/supreme-court-agrees-to-drop-criminal-proceedings-against-fugitive-sandesara-brothers-if-they-paid-rs-5100-crore-503463-2025-11-24>
- <https://www.livelaw.in/amp/top-stories/sandesarasterling-group-loan-fraud-supreme-court-quashes-criminal-cases-after-accused-agree-to-pay-rs-5100-crore-to-banks-311087>
- <https://www.moneylife.in/article/sterling-biotech-case-sc-questions-sebi-over-continued-probe-into-sandesara-brothers-despite-5100-crore-settlement/79966.html>
